candidate_relations.reason: The benchmark specifically identifies 'Window-Period Acute Myocardial Infarction,' referring to the hyperacute phase characterized by tall upright T waves (hyperacute T waves) before troponin elevation and before ST changes fully evolve — a time-sensitive ECG diagnosis. C001 correctly identifies ACS with the LAD occlusion anatomy but uses the broader parent category 'Acute Coronary Syndrome' without specifying the window-period/hyperacute AMI phase, which is the critical diagnostic specificity required by the benchmark.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: ACS is the parent category encompassing STEMI, NSTEMI, and unstable angina; it does not specify the window-period (hyperacute) phase of AMI that is the benchmark diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Benchmark diagnosis 'Window-Period AMI' hinges on hyperacute T-wave pattern with negative troponin, representing the earliest recognizable ECG phase of STEMI equivalent before biomarker rise — a nuanced time-state diagnosis not captured by the generic ACS label in C001
